ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Revelation is wholly governed by God: the Prophet neither acquires it at will nor can refuse or retain it if God removes it; it is a divine bounty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he does not even have the power to keep it with him if God wanted to take it away

BURSEVI:v5p155/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p155/r1.claim: The first lām introduces an unspoken oath and the second marks its answer; the answer also serves the conditional clause.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r1.anchor: اللام الأولى موطئة للقسم المحذوف والثانية لام الجواب وهذا الجواب ساد مسد جوابي القسم والشرط

BURSEVI:v5p155/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p155/r2.claim: The hypothetical removal means erasing the Qur'an from copies and hearts, leaving the Prophet as before without knowledge of scripture; it is a supposition for argument.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r2.anchor: ذهبنا بالقرآن ومحوناه من المصاحف والصدور فلم نترك منه أثرا

BURSEVI:v5p155/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p155/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p155/r3.claim: After the Qur'an's removal, no one could act as an advocate to recover it or restore its copies and memorized form.
BURSEVI:v5p155/r3.anchor: كما قال الكاشفي : (س نيابي تو براي خود بآن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r1.claim: The revealed thing that God could take away is the Quran, with its healing and mercy and the revelation by which God steadied the Prophet when opponents nearly diverted him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r1.anchor: من القرآن الذي هو شفاء ورحمة للمؤمنين والذي ثبتناك عليه حين كادوا يفتنونك عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r2.claim: The relative expression magnifies the Quran and describes its status from the outset, showing it is not the speech of a created being.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r2.anchor: وإنما عبر عنه بالموصول تفخيما لشأنه ووصفا له بما في حيز الصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r3.claim: The first lām introduces an oath, and the following promise answers that oath rather than serving as the conditional clause; this permits omission of the object after 'if We willed'.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r3.anchor: واللام الأولى موطئة للقسم ( ولنذهبن ) جوابه النائب مناب جزاء الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r4.claim: Taking the Quran away means erasing it from manuscripts and memories, whether as written forms or stored mental images; no advocate could guarantee its restoration, and الوكيل is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p164/r4.anchor: ويراد بالذهاب به محوه عن المصاحف والصدرور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r1.claim: The revelation that God could take away is the Qur'an; as with the withheld knowledge about the spirit, God could remove it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r1.anchor: {ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك} يعني القرآن. معناه: إنا كما منعنا علم الروح عنك وعن غيرك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r2.claim: A wakīl who could restore the Qur'an would be one entrusted to bring it back against God's will, and none exists.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126#2/r2.anchor: {ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا} أي: من يتوكل برد القرآن إليك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r1.claim: If God willed, He could remove the revelation, erasing the Qur'an from manuscripts and memories; the oath lām introduces the conditional oath's answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r1.anchor: اللام الأولى موطئة للقسم و { لنذهبن } جوابه النائب مناب جزاء الشرط.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r2.claim: No one could act as an advocate to restore it to the Prophet, written or memorized.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:86-88/r2.anchor: ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا } من يتوكل علينا استرداده مسطورا محفوظا.

QASHANI:17:85-87/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r3.claim: God could remove revelation by effacement in annihilation or veil it after disclosure through spiritual fluctuation, with no agent able to restore it.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r3.anchor: بالطمس في محل الفناء أو الحجب بعد الكشف بالتلوين

QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.claim: A direct manifestation of the divine essence would leave neither revelation nor the Prophet's self; manifestation through mercy brings both into being, while majesty can veil revelation and knowledge.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r5.anchor: لو تجلينا بذاتنا لما وجدت الوحي ولا ذاتك إلا إذا تجلينا بصفة الرحمة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r1.claim: After describing attempts to alter revelation and expel the Messenger, the verse warns that God could remove the Qur’an and leave people with their little knowledge and ignorance.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r1.anchor: تنبيها لهم على أنه لو شاء لذهب بسبب هذا العلم القليل الذي وهبهموه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r2.claim: No protector could bring the revelation back against God; the emphatic oath construction answers the conditional by asserting certain removal if God willed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r2.anchor: ولامه موطئة للقسم , وأجاب عن القسم بما أغنى عن جواب الشرط

BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r3.claim: The phrasing emphasizes the revelation’s subject; the author says God alone can restore or replace it by mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p423/r3.anchor: أي لكن تجد { رحمة } مبتدئة وكائنة { من ربك } أي المحسن إليك

DURR-FULL:v5p333/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r4.claim: A Yemen delegation challenges the Prophet with a riddle, tests his prophethood through speaking pebbles, then hears him recite; moved to tears, he says he fears straying from the razor-edged path on which God sent him, and recites the warning that revelation could be taken away.
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لما قدم وفد اليمن على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: أبيت اللعن

DURR-FULL:v5p333/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says the Qur'an will be taken in one night from every heart and written copy, leaving people with none of it.
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن هذا القرآن سيرفع قيل: كيف يرفع وقد أثبته الله في قلوبنا

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says the Qur'an will be removed from every codex in a night.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: ليسرين على القرآن في ليلة فلا يترك آية في مصحف أحد إلا رفعت

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the Qur'an will disappear from people's insides, leaving nothing of it on earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: يسر ى على القرآن ليلا فيذهب به من أجواف الرجال

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r3.claim: Ibn Masud urges reciting before the Qur'an is raised from hearts at night, after which people forget knowledge and turn to poetry.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: اقرؤوا القرآن قبل أن يرفع فإنه لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرفع

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r4.claim: The Prophet says Islam will wear away like a garment and the Book of God will be taken in one night; only elderly people repeating the testimony remain, unaware of prayer, fasting, or rites.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r4.anchor: عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يدرس الإسلام كما يدرس وشي الثوب

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r5.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r5.claim: Hudhayfa says Islam will wear away, the Qur'an will lose its sweetness and be removed overnight from hearts, and people will forget prayer, fasting, and rites.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r5.anchor: عن حذيفة رضي الله عنه قال: يوشك أن يدرس الإسلام كما يدرس وشي الثوب ويقرأ الناس القرآن لا يجدون له حلاوة

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r6.speaker: شمر بن عطية
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r6.claim: Shamr ibn Atiya says the Qur'an will be lifted overnight, leaving night worshippers unable to recite from memory or copies; they will gather and report the loss to one another.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r6.anchor: عن شمر بن عطية رضي الله عنه قال: يسرى على القران في ليلة فيقوم المتهجدون في ساعاتهم فلا يقدرون على شيء

DURR-FULL:v5p334/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a Prophetic report that a time will come when the Qur'an is sent for and lifted from earth.
DURR-FULL:v5p334/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يأتي الناس زمان يرسل إلى القرآن ويرفع من الأرض

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r1.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says the Qur'an will be lifted from its place of descent, sounding around the Throne like bees and protesting that it was recited but not acted upon.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه قال: لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرفع القرآن من حيث نزل له دوي حول العرش

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r2.speaker: الليث بن سعد
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r2.claim: Al-Layth ibn Sad says the Qur'an is lifted when people turn to other books and abandon it.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r2.anchor: عن الليث بن سعد رضي الله عنه قال: إنما يرفع القرآن حين يقبل الناس على الكتب ويكبون عليها

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r3.claim: The Prophet commands adherence to God's Book after his departure and warns that the Qur'an will be removed overnight from hearts and copies.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r3.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنه قال: خرج علينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أطيعوني ما دمت بين أظهركم

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra says the Book will be lifted to heaven along with the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms, leaving people unable to know what they are doing in prayer.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: يسرى على كتاب الله فيرفع إلى السماء فلا يبقى على الأرض من القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r5.claim: Hudhayfa and Abu Hurayra transmit that the Book will be lifted at night, leaving no verse on earth or in a Muslim's body.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r5.anchor: عن حذيفة وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يسرى على كتاب الله ليلا

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r6.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying the Hour will not come until remembrance and Qur'an are lifted.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r6.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تقوم الساعة حتى يرفع الذكر والقرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p335/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar say the Prophet warned against writing other books alongside God's Book; God may remove it overnight from hearts and pages, leaving the testimony of faith in whomever He wills good.
DURR-FULL:v5p335/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن عمر رضي الله عنها قالا: خطب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا أيها الناس ما هذه الكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.claim: The warning follows the Quran’s healing and mercy: knowledge should prompt gratitude, not conceit, since God can withdraw it; this cautions the Prophet and, by extension, other scholars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r1.anchor: أعقب ذلك بالتنبيه إلى الشكر على نعمة العلم دفعا لغرور النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.claim: The statement explicitly warns of removal but indirectly expresses favor, as the next verse explains; the Prophet is addressed because his knowledge is greatest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r2.anchor: فالكلام صريحه تحذير ، وهو كناية عن الامتنان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r3.claim: The lām introduces an unspoken oath, and the emphatic future verb answers that oath and thereby supplies the conditional answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r3.anchor: واللام موطئة للقسم المحذوف قبل الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r4.claim: The oath response also supplies the conditional answer, so no separate conditional response is needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r4.anchor: وهو دليل جواب الشرط ومغن عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r5.claim: ثم orders the denial of any recovery by rhetorical rank, since inability to regain the lost revelation is more grievous than losing it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r5.anchor: و ( ثم ) للترتيب الرتبي ، لأن نفي الطمع في استرجاع المسلوب أشد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r6.claim: وكيل is one entrusted with a task; here it means defender, intercessor, or advocate able to secure restoration of the revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p200/r6.anchor: والوكيل : من يوكل إليه المهم . والمراد به هنا المدافع عنك والشفيع لك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r11.claim: The warning rebukes the Prophet for promising an answer the next day; he must submit to God’s choice of what to reveal or withhold.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r11.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولئن شئنا الآية فيها شدة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي عتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports a red wind from Syria removing Qurʾān from codices and hearts, citing this verse to show it is possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r12.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أنه ستخرج ريح حمراء من قبل الشام فتزيل القرآن من المصاحف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r13.claim: Wakīl is one who manages an affair, including advocacy, dispute, or arranging benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r13.anchor: و «الوكيل» القائم بالأمر في الانتصار أو المخاصمة ونحو ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r1.claim: God could erase the revelation from hearts and books until no trace remained, leaving no one able to retrieve any of it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى لو شئنا لمحوناه من القلوب والكتب حتى لا يوجد له أثر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r5.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r5.claim: Wakīl means someone who would defend the Prophet against God’s decision to remove the revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r5.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان ثم لا تجد لك به أي بما نفعله بك من إذهاب ما عندك وكيلا يدفعنا عما نريده بك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r6.claim: A report says Gabriel would remove the Quran from people’s breasts and homes in one night, so they would wake unable to recite or sense a verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r6.anchor: وروي عن عبدالله ابن مسعود انه قال يسرى على القرآن في ليلة واحدة فيجيء جبريل من جوف الليل فيذهب به من صدورهم ومن بيوتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r7.claim: Al-Dimashqī rejects the report’s soundness because the Prophet said knowledge is not seized by sudden extraction; sound chains for Ibn Masʿūd’s report may mean knowledge other than Quran, whose removal would come last.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p83/r7.anchor: ورد أبو سليمان الدمشقي صحة هذا الحديث بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام ان الله لا يقبض العلم انتزاعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says a red wind from Syria will come at the end of time, erasing every Quran verse from people's codices and hearts; he recited this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r1.anchor: قال ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه: يطرق الناس ريح حمراء -يعني في آخر الزمان -من قبل الشام،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r2.claim: God reminds Muhammad that the revealed Quran is a great favor, and that no combination of humans and jinn, even cooperating, can produce its like because created speech cannot match the Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p117/r2.anchor: أنه لو اجتمعت الإنس والجن كلهم، واتفقوا (1) على أن يأتوا بمثل ما أنزله على رسوله،

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r6.claim: A wakil is someone entrusted with affairs and relied upon.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r6.anchor: والوكيل: من وكلت الأمور إليه، واعتمدت عليه.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r8.claim: God could erase revelation from hearts and books until no trace remained, leaving the Prophet no protector to restore it; terms may mean defender, guarantor, or keeper.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r8.anchor: قيل: بمحونا من القلوب والكتب حتى لا يبقى له أثر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r1.claim: God could remove revelation from hearts and written copies so people could no longer access it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r1.anchor: لأذهبناه من الصدور والكتب حتى لا يقدر عليه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r2.claim: Alternatively, God could take Muhammad in death, ending further revelation to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r2.anchor: لأذهبناه بقبضك إلينا حتى لا ينزل عليك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r3.claim: If revelation were removed, no one could undertake to restore it; this fits the first interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r3.anchor: أي لا تجد من يتوكل في رده إليك , وهو تأويل من قال بالوجه الأول .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r4.claim: Alternatively, no one could protect Muhammad from God; this fits the second interpretation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p271/r4.anchor: الثاني : لا تجد من يمنعنا منك , وهو تأويل من قال بالوجه الثاني .

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r5.claim: When the Prophet was invited to his forefathers' religion, God warned He could take away the Qur'an, with no protector able to prevent Him.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r5.anchor: وذلك حين دعي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى دين آبائه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r1.claim: This passage recalls the gift of revelation and consoles the Prophet to endure argumentative questioning.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r1.anchor: ثم نبه على نعمة الوحى وعزاء بالصبر على أذى الجدال في السؤال بقوله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r2.claim: The lām is preparatory to an omitted oath and stands in place of the conditional answer: if God willed, He could erase the Qurʾān from hearts and codices without leaving a trace.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r2.anchor: لنذهبن جواب قسم محذوف مع نيابته عن جزاء الشرط واللام الداخلة على ان توطئة للقسم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r3.claim: After its removal the Prophet would find no one to restore the revelation, memorized or written, by interceding with God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا ﴾ أي ثم لا تجد لك بعد الذهاب به من يتوكل علينا بإسترداده وإعادته

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.claim: After granting people little knowledge, God says He could remove even that by erasing its memory from hearts and its written traces from books, despite this being extraordinary.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r1.anchor: يمحو حفظه من القلوب وكتابته من الكتب

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.claim: Al-Ka'bi argues that the Quran is created because anything God can remove cannot be eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r2.anchor: احتج الكعبي بهذه الآية على أن القرآن مخلوق

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.claim: Razi calls that inference remote: removing knowledge from hearts and inscriptions from manuscripts does not show that the known or signified Quran is created.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r3.anchor: وذلك لا يوجب كون ذلك المعلوم المدلول محدثا

RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.claim: The clause about finding no agent means there would be no one to rely on to restore any part of the revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v21p45#2/r4.anchor: أي لا تجد من تتوكل عليه في رد شيء منه

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.claim: Although the verses use singular address, verse 86 is read as addressing everyone or the Prophet and community, while the final sentence of verse 87 is addressed to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r1.anchor: most commentators read v. 86 as addressed to people in general

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r3.claim: After the previous verse says people received little knowledge, this warns that even that little knowledge could be taken away.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r3.anchor: In v. 85, human beings are said to have been given only a little knowledge

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r4.claim: Taking away revelation can mean removing the Quran from human memory and written copies.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r4.anchor: That God might take away what He had revealed is said to refer to His ability to remove the Quran completely from human access

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r5.speaker: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says religion will first lose trust and last lose prayer; the Quran will then be lifted overnight from written copies and hearts.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r5.anchor: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd (d. ca. 29/650) said, “The first thing that will be lost from your religion is trust

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r6.speaker: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the Hour will not arrive until the Quran is returned to where it descended; when returned, it will complain that people recited but did not follow it.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r6.anchor: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar (d. 74/693), the son of the second Caliph, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, is reported to have said

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r7.claim: Without revelation, no guardian could return the Quran; the exception of mercy may mean God chooses not to remove it or restores it after removal.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r7.anchor: The exception save a mercy means either that God might choose not to remove it

STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.claim: These warning and exception express God's mercy in revealing and preserving the Quran in people's hearts and writing; mercy and bounty are paired elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:17:86/r8.anchor: Both the warning and the exception indicate that God’s Mercy is manifested not only in revealing the Quran

TAB-FULL:v15p74/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r1.claim: If God removed the revelation, no guardian could protect it and no supporter could prevent Him; wakil means a caretaker or protector.
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r1.anchor: قيما يقوم لك، فيمنعنا من فعل ذلك بك، ولا ناصرا ينصرك، فيحول بيننا وبين ما نريد بك،

TAB-FULL:v15p74/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r2.claim: Ibn Masud interprets God's taking the revelation as the Qur'an being lifted from the hearts and copies of its reciters.
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r2.anchor: قال: قلت لعبد الله، وذكر أنه يسرى على القرآن: كيف وقد أثبتناه في صدورنا ومصاحفنا؟ قال: يسرى عليه ليلا،

TAB-FULL:v15p74/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says a red wind from Syria will erase every Qur'anic verse from copies and hearts, even from someone who had collected it.
TAB-FULL:v15p74/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، قال: تطرق الناس ريح حمراء من نحو الشام، فلا يبقى في مصحف رجل ولا قلبه آية.

TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.claim: The following verse about removing revelation does not uniquely support the Quran interpretation; it also fits other proposed meanings of spirit.
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.anchor: على أن الآية التالية لا تتعين تأييدا لهذا الوجه بل تلائم بعض الوجوه الأخر أيضا

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r6.claim: In context the revelation that God could remove is the heavenly Spirit carrying the Quran; no advocate could demand its return or compel God to restore it.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r6.anchor: الروح النازل عليك الملقي بالقرآن إليك من أمرنا غير خارج من قدرتنا

TABATABAI:17:86-89/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r1.claim: The ‘revealed’ thing is the divine Spirit sent to the Prophet, as in 42:52; the ‘advocate’ is one who demands its return, not a custodian preserving or reciting the Quran.
TABATABAI:17:86-89/r1.anchor: المراد بالوكيل للمطالبة والرد لما أذهبه الله دون الوكيل في حفظ القرآن وتلاوته

TABRISI:17:85-87/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85-87/r10.claim: God could remove the Qurʾān He revealed but, through mercy, gave the Prophet what he needed and withheld details he did not need, even if people mistakenly thought them necessary.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r10.anchor: يعني القرآن ومعناه أني أقدر أن آخذ ما أعطيتك كما منعت غيرك

TABRISI:17:85-87/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r11.speaker: الحسن وأبو مسلم والأصم
TABRISI:17:85-87/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Muslim, and al-Aṣamm say God could erase the Qurʾān from the Prophet’s and community’s memories, leaving no trace or keeper.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r11.anchor: حتى لا يوجد له أثر ثم لا تجد له حفيظا يحفظه عليك

TABRISI:17:85-87/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85-87/r12.claim: The erasure interpretation is evidence that the question about spirit concerned the Qurʾān.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r12.anchor: عن الحسن وأبي مسلم والأصم قالوا وفي هذا دلالة على أن السؤال وقع عن القرآن

THALABI:v6p130#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p130#2/r9.claim: “What We revealed” means the Qur'an; a “guardian” would be a supporter who could protect and restore it.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r9.anchor: ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك يعني القرآن ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا ناصرا

THALABI:v6p130#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p130#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says a guardian is one who could protect the Prophet from God if God wished to take the revelation.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن: وكيلا ناصرا يمنعك منا إذا أردناك

THALABI:v6p131/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p131/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v6p131/r1.claim: The Prophet says that whoever God intends good for will retain “There is no god but God” in the heart when other written material is removed.
THALABI:v6p131/r1.anchor: قالوا: يا رسول الله فكيف بالمؤمنين والمؤمنات يومئذ؟ قال: «من أراد الله به خيرا

THALABI:v6p131/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p131/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v6p131/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says trust is the first religious duty to disappear, prayer and praying people the last; the Qur'an will be withdrawn from hearts and codices in one night, leaving people like beasts.
THALABI:v6p131/r2.anchor: وروى شداد بن معقل عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: إن أول ما تفقدون من دينكم الأمانة

THALABI:v6p131/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p131/r3.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v6p131/r3.claim: A report from Abdullah urges abundant pilgrimage and recitation before the Qur'an is removed overnight and people forget the declaration of faith and follow pre-Islamic customs.
THALABI:v6p131/r3.anchor: وروى موسى بن عبيدة عن صفوان بن سليم عن ناجية بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن أبيه عن عبد الله

THALABI:v6p131/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p131/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
THALABI:v6p131/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the Qur'an will be raised at the end of time after people recite it without acting on it.
THALABI:v6p131/r4.anchor: عبد الله بن عمرو قال: لا يقوم الساعة حتى يرفع القرآن من حيث نزل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.claim: Alternatively, the address may concern the Prophet and believers, whose knowledge of the spirit was not disclosed; the following threat to withdraw revelation supports this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.anchor: لم يبين الله له ذلك، قال له:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r1.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r1.claim: The first lām in la-in is emphatic rather than the oath's answer; lanadhhabanna supplies the answer and receives the oath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r1.anchor: وإنما الجواب: لنذهبن، وعليه وقع الحلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r2.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r2.claim: The first lām may be omitted while the second lām answers the oath, as in the cited Qur'anic example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r2.anchor: جواز سقوط الأولى في قوله تعالى: {وإن لم ينتهوا عما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r3.claim: God is able to take back what He gave the Prophet, consistent with his having received only a little knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r3.anchor: لم تؤت إلا قليلا من العلم، وإن شئت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r4.claim: God could erase revelation from hearts and books until no trace remained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r4.anchor: لو شئنا لمحونا من القلوب ومن الكتب حتى لا يوجد له أثر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r5.claim: A wakīl would be someone who could be relied upon to restore any of the withdrawn revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p471/r5.anchor: أي: لا تجد من يتوكل عليه في رد شيء منه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:86/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:86/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:86/r1.claim: If God willed, He could erase revelation from hearts and books until no trace remained; the Prophet would have no one to rely on to restore it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:86/r1.anchor: لنمحونه من القلوب ومن الكتب حتى لا يوجد له أثر { ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا } لا تجد من تتوكل عليه في رد شيء منه.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r4.claim: God could take away the Qur’an entirely so that not even a part of it remained.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r4.anchor: قوله: {ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك} [الإسراء: 86] ، يعني القرآن حتى لا يبقى منه شيء.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r5.claim: No guardian could prevent God from taking it away.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r5.anchor: ثم لا تجد لك به علينا وكيلا} [الإسراء: 86] وليا يمنعك من ذلك.

ELMALILI:17:86-87/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r1.claim: God swears He could erase from memory all the Qur’an revealed through the Holy Spirit, preserved against trials, and serving believers as healing and the spirit of knowledge; no advocate could retrieve it.
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r1.anchor: o sana vahyettiğimizi elbet gideriveririz. Yani Rûhu’l-kudüs’le indirdiğimiz, bütün fitnelere karşı tesbit ettiğimiz

ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.claim: Except for mercy from the Lord, the Prophet can rely on no one; the same Lord who revealed the Qur’an preserves it and sustains him through a special grace meant to spread universal mercy.
ELMALILI:17:86-87/r2.anchor: ancak Rabbinden bir rahmet evvel ü âhir yalnız O’na dayanabilirsin ve işte onu vahyettiğimiz gibi, hıfz u ibkā eden de O’dur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.claim: The phrase rendered “you will find no protector against Us” can also mean finding no supporter or helper able to restore revelation to the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r1.anchor: onu sana geri verebilecek bir destekçi, yardımcı bulamazsın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.claim: All knowledge comes from God; He could cause the Prophet and later generations to forget revelation, and no other power could protect, restore, or replace it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r2.anchor: Dilerse gönderdiği vahyi Peygamber’e ve sonra gelen nesillere unutturmak suretiyle

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.claim: Earlier scriptures were largely forgotten or partly altered by people, illustrating their inability to secure divine knowledge by themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:86/r3.anchor: Kur’an’dan önceki kutsal kitapların büyük bir kısmı tamamen, bazısı da kısmen unutulmuş

ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r1.claim: If God willed, He could erase the revelation from hearts and books until no trace remained.
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r1.anchor: أي لو شئنا لمحوناه من القلوب ومن الكتب حتى لا يوجد له أثر

ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r2.claim: No one could then act as guarantor to restore any of it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p258/r2.anchor: أي لاتجد من يتوكل في رد شيء منه.

ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r1.claim: No one could provide the Prophet an alternative guide, since divine revelation is the sole absolute source of ethics.
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r1.anchor: divine guidance is the only source of ethics in the absolute sense of this word

ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r2.claim: Taking revelation away means removing it from people's hearts and memories as well as erasing it in written form.
ASAD-NOTES:17:86#n102/r2.anchor: its alienation from the hearts and the memory of men, as well as its disappearance in written form

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r11.claim: After mentioning the gift of revelation, God says He could take it away if He willed, though He did not; the power to send it includes power to remove it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r11.anchor: أنا كما نحن قادرون على إنزاله نحن قادرون على إذهابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r12.speaker: أبو سهل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r12.claim: Abu Sahl reads the warning as directed to others, threatening removal of what they possess to deter questions about knowledge not granted, such as the spirit or Hour.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r12.anchor: هذا تهديد لغير الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بإذهاب ما أوتوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r1.claim: Reports say the Qur'an will be lifted before the Hour; Ibn Masud's hadith says it is removed in one night from manuscripts and hearts, then he recited this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r1.anchor: وفي حديث ابن مسعود يسرى به في ليلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r2.speaker: صاحب التحرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r2.claim: The author of al-Tahrir proposes that delayed revelation about the spirit distressed Muhammad, so this verse consoled him by reminding him that God could remove all revelation; the Prophet was reassured and learned decorum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r2.anchor: لما أبطأ عليه الوحي لما سئل عن الروح شق ذلك عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r3.claim: The preposition ba in lanadhhaban bihi is causative, like the hamza in a causative verb, as discussed at the start of al-Baqara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r3.anchor: والباء في لنذهبن بالذي للتعدية كالهمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r4.claim: Wakil may mean one who preserves the revelation, guarantees its return to hearts, or guarantees that God will restore what was taken.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r4.anchor: والكفيل هنا قيل من يحفظ ما أوحينا إليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says God could erase the Qur'an from hearts and manuscripts, leaving the Prophet with no knowledge of the Book and no guarantor to restore it, except by God's mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p107/r5.anchor: محوناه عن الصدور والمصاحف ولم نترك له أثرا
